verdict: Nike's revenue rose 1% to $12.4B — wholesale grew 8% and North America 9%, but Nike Direct fell 8% and Greater China 17% — and higher tariffs cut the gross margin by three points, dropping profit 32% to $792M.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — the growth engine this quarter, on wholesale demand.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Europe, the Middle East and Africa — up on reported numbers, down 1% without currency help.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: Asia-Pacific (outside Greater China) and Latin America.

segments.name: Greater China
segments.note: China — down hard (-16% without currency help) as footwear fell 21%.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Converse sneaker brand — down across all territories.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Global brand divisions plus corporate leftovers (mostly currency-hedge results).

opex.name: Demand creation
opex.note: Advertising and sports marketing — up 13%, with higher brand marketing and sports marketing.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Salaries, technology and running the business — down 4% on lower wage-related and administrative costs.

takeaways.title: Wholesale carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 1% to $12.4B (flat without currency help). Wholesale revenue grew 8% and North America 9%, but Nike Direct fell 8% — digital sales dropped 14% — and Greater China fell 17%.

takeaways.title: Tariffs squeezed the margin
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell 300 basis points to 40.6%, primarily on higher tariffs in North America. Inventories were $7.7B, down 3% — fewer units, but carrying higher tariff-driven product costs.

takeaways.title: Profit fell 32%
takeaways.text: Net income fell 32% to $792M and EPS to $0.53. Demand creation spending rose 13% as Nike leans into brand marketing for its 'Win Now' reset, while operating overhead fell 4%.

otherDetail: $9M of net interest income, less $16M of other expense, net.
footerNote: Segment revenues are Nike's divisional revenues; 'Global Brand & Corporate' combines Global Brand Divisions ($9M) and Corporate ($3M).
